beats.narration: [excited] One wheel. One night. Millions gone.
[thoughtful] Monte Carlo, August nineteen thirteen. Black hit twenty-six times in a row. [whispers] The room started chasing red. They said red was due.

[confident] The wheel has no memory. Ask the odds of black on spin twenty-seven. Divide the chance of twenty-seven blacks by the twenty-six that already fell. The powers cancel. Eighteen over thirty-seven remains. Same as spin one. Every bet against black chased a number that had already come true.
[warm] That fallacy still fires. Slot pulls. Coin flips. Your brain sees a pattern. The wheel does not.
